utterances.text: We - that is the working group - have not established that. That may have been established, as far as I know, by members of the expert team. From what I know from speaking to them at the time, the bodies do not date back to a long time ago. They date back to a recent time. There is no great difference between their times of death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Karleusa. In addition to a great number of discrepancies and clarities, ambiguities, you took only a few days, allegedly, to establish the relevant facts and hold a press conference, and created an impression that the bodies concerned were from Kosovo. So I'm asking you now, was it a politically motivated campaign which should have served as a preparation, as paving the way for my illegal extradition to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We gave a press release when we gave it, and neither I nor anyone else from my working group was motivated by political agendas that you mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since you yesterday talked about the composition of the working group and from that composition, without naming any names, we can see that there were two lieutenant colonels and one major in that working group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So two lieutenant colonels and one major. Does it seem logical to you, that you as a captain, the lowest ranking member of that working group, be the leader of that group, superior to the lieutenant colonels and the major?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was leader of that working group not because I was captain by rank but because I was deputy head of the criminal investigations police force at the time, and I don't see anything irregular or illogical about the fact that I was the leader of the working group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it have to do anything with the fact that professionally and otherwise, in business terms, you were related to the then Minister Dusan Mihajlovic, bypassing regular official links?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me then, Mr. Karleusa, is it true that the enterprise whose co-owner is your wife is engaged in supplying private companies owned by Dusan Mihajlovic, your minister? Supplying security guards.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is not true, that your wife does not co-own this enterprise, this company --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's enough. It has nothing to do with this trial. You've heard what this witness has said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. Here is an exhibit. The registration with the business relations court in Belgrade of an enterprise which names among its activities physical and technical security services. Fito Centar is his name. Svetlana, father's name Jan, Karleusa. That's your wife, isn't she?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Address Pariske Komune 61. Here we read: "Unlimited Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 8450 to 8458. authorisations," and so on and so forth. Svetlana Karleusa, acting director without limitation of authority, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has answered. He said it has nothing to do with his evidence or the fact that he was made the leader of the group. Now, that's his answer. The fact that his wife may have had a relationship with somebody else is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, it is very relevant what kind of relationship he has with the current member of the government and his own minister, apart from the fact that he is employed with the MUP, and all these parallel links are very relevant because it is precisely that government which is extremely involved in what I call self-humiliation and self-degradation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know that political speeches are not allowed here. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, what is suggested is this, and perhaps we could deal with it in various forms: First of all, does your wife have this company? Is she a director of this company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She is co-owner and director of that company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the Minister of the Interior, what is his involvement with it? So we can understand the position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That company that is managed by my wife does not provide security for any companies or premises that have anything to do with Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there any business relationship between them at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be suggested that your evidence in this case is affected in some way by some sort of relationship, business relationship of some sort. Is there any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There is no truth in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. You can ask two more questions and then your time is up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. That is customary practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now answer me a question that has to do with the end of your statement. I'm going to read the last paragraph to you: "I have been advised that my statement may be sought by other law enforcement agencies and/or judicial authorities for the purpose of prosecution." Full stop. And then another sentence: "I hereby do not," underlined, "do not agree to the release of any part of my statement to such authorities at the discretion of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia." And you speak of their discretion. Why do you not give this agreement, Mr. Karleusa? Is it because the sole purpose of this is for testifying in this trial, this illegal trial against me, or is there some other reason for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I gave this statement, I used my own words, and they are, for the most part, contained in that statement. At the end of that statement, as far as I can see, it says that I am not giving the kind of agreement that you have just referred to, as it has been put here. However, I did not understand that or have I ever heard of any such situation existing. This did not pertain to Yugoslav judicial authorities, because Yugoslav judicial authorities, starting from the court of law and the prosecutor's office, can obtain this at any point in time, because my statement is in the hands of the National Committee of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for Cooperation with the Hague Tribunal, then also the team that works at the level of the Ministry of the Interior. And I thought at that time that that was supposed to mean that it is not supposed to be made public. I did not know how all of this would evolve, but it is true that that's what I said so let me explain now what I meant by it. That's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, Mr. Karleusa, in view of such an alleged operation of removing corpses that is being ascribed to the very top echelons of the state, does it seem to you that such a decision can be made by any sensible person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, that's a comment. Mr. Karleusa, you needn't deal with that. That's something, Mr. Milosevic, that we will have to consider. You can make that point to us in due course. Now, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Dealing with paragraph 8 of the summary, last sentence in paragraph 8. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, you gave evidence today that you saw a statement by Rade Markovic in which information was contained that Mr. Milosevic had ordered the removal of crimes from the Kosovo area. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm looking at a statement made by you this year, which was an interview on the 27th of May, 2002, and the 3rd of June, 2002, and in that statement you recite the same fact about Mr. Milosevic's order, but you say in the statement: "I am not certain of the source of this information, although I was advised of this at a MUP meeting. It was my understanding that the information most likely came from one of the participants of the Milosevic meeting." Can you explain the contradiction between your statement that I've just read out and the evidence you gave today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I gave my statement to Mr. John Zdrilic, investigator, I did not wish to state the source, knowing that the document bore the marking "strictly confidential." At that moment, I thought I was not allowed to disclose the source. Later, I saw that I could state that and that that is not contestable, so I did that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions. Re-examined by Mr. Shin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, do you recall approximately when the accused arrived at The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On St. Vitus's Day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what year was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigations that were carried out regarding the refrigerator truck by the working group, did they continue after that date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they continuing currently, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are continuing upon instructions of the prosecutor's office in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who or what organ is carrying out those investigations apart from the prosecutor's office which you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the request of the prosecutor in charge, regardless of whether it is a case of Belgrade, Negotin, or Uzice, the collection of information that is required is being carried out by a department for combatting organised crime, and it is within the ministry, as I've already mentioned. It is called the Department for the Investigation of War Crimes and Searching for Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still in -- are you still in charge of these investigations? Are you personally still in charge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not in charge personally, but since I am deputy head of the administration within which this department is, I am indirectly involved. But I am not directly engaged in carrying out any investigation nor am I regularly informed about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the working group still in existence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The working group no longer exists in that form and with that membership as was the case then. All of the tasks carried out by that working group have now been incorporated into the department I've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had mentioned in your direct testimony that exhumations are continuing this summer, even now, at least with respect to one site in Batajnica. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you aware of other exhumations that will be carried out in the future? Just if you know. I'm sorry, I -- just to explain, exhumations in connection with the three sites you mentioned; Batajnica, Petrovo Selo, and Perucac Lake.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know and as far as the working group knew, it is possible that other exhumations will take place in the Batajnica locality. That is what we stated. And the exhumations will probably go on until this locality and this terrain are fully searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karleusa, with regards to the March 1999 meeting, I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Usher, if you could, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the document carefully, and I will ask you some questions after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, would it be possible to have this document marked for identification? The Prosecution intends to put this document in as evidence through a later witness and this is a document that is in fact the subject of disclosure today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the document first? Tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: The document is a statement that Radomir Markovic provided to -- to the police in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness can identify it first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could just ask him some questions then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, do you recall having seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have not seen this document in this form before. What I did see is a similar statement but in different form at the meeting that I referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, what is the date of this document that you see before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 2nd of June, 2001 or 2002. I can't see exactly. 2002. 2001. It says in the text the 2nd of June, 2001, whereas what is handwritten is a bit illegible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, could you explain very briefly what this document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must rise here. It's not his document, he doesn't recognise the document, and I'm not sure what the purpose of this exercise is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, I don't think you can really take this any further. You can, of course, deal with it with another witness, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What I would seek to ask the witness is whether from what he has seen here, whether it's consistent with the document that he has testified that he saw prior to his communique in May of -- I believe that was 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But he said it's similar. Perhaps you could ask this: Were the contents of the document similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. The contents of this document are, for the most part, the same or similar to the document that I had seen and on the basis of which we gave our statement and on the basis of which our knowledge was obtained. However, the form was different. I think that that particular record was different. It had more pages, not devoted to this subject but perhaps to something else. I saw only that which pertained to questions related to my own province of work. So that's about it. Perhaps there is a bit more here or perhaps I do not remember enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think you can take it any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If I could please just have that document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, I don't think you can for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was just going to raise a matter concerning the date which the Prosecution should perhaps look at again on the second page and third page of the document for the year; 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The witness can't identify it. Let the Prosecution have the document back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Office of the Prosecutor has very recently received a report from the Spanish National Institute of Toxicology, within the past week, which will explain the results of some of the DNA samples that Witness William Fulton testified about and will indicate that the bodies found in that Batajnica site do -- to a high degree of probability do relate to persons from Kosovo. I'm not sure how Your Honours would like us to proceed with this. We could, for example, have another investigator come in to put in these documents, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That might be the most efficient way to deal with it and there can be any examination about it. This witness can't clearly deal it because he doesn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Bosko Radojkovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, apparently a milestone has been reached with the calling of this witness: 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I had the earphones on and, unfortunately, it was a different channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was just saying that a milestone has been reached in the Prosecution's case: This is the 100th witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out. I'm sorry, I lost track of the numbers. 100. Thank you. If it assists while we're waiting for the witness, Your Honours, during the course of his evidence I do intend to show him a series of some ten photographs in a bundle, and the Court may in fact have already received a copy of those photographs, along with the summary which I prepared, in advance. And does the Registrar have copies available now or do we -- I'm just trying to save time, if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat. Examined by Mr. Ryneveld:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, could you state your full name for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Bosko Radojkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that you're 46 years of age and you're currently a policeman employed as a senior crime technician in the Serbian Ministry of Interior in Kladovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the course of your duties as a crime technician or a crime scene identification officer, do they include such things as taking photographs and fingerprints and attending the scene of what are suspected to be crimes?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long have you been doing that kind of work with the police in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Twenty-five years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your career as a crime scene examiner, sir, have you had any experience with bodies that have been in water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, is there a particular body of water with which you have had considerable experience in terms of finding bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the place where I work, it mainly had to do with corpses in the river of the Danube, the Danube River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of your duties, sir, I take it you found various bodies that had been dead ranging from fairly recent to long periods of time?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of your duties, did you ever have the occasion to tentatively give estimates of how long these bodies had been in water, or had been dead?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, together with the doctor and the rest of the team which conducted the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's in generality. I'd like you now, if you would, please, to turn your mind to an incident on the 5th of April of 1999. In the course of your duties, were you called upon to attend the scene in the Danube River near the village of Tekija near Kladovo? Or Tekija.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, sir, about how it is that you went to the scene of the Danube River and what is it that you saw when you arrived on the 5th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The police officer on duty informed me that in the Danube River near Tekija village, a fisherman noticed an object floating on the water, something that looked like a trailer box on a truck. Since it was not unusual for vehicles to skid off the road and into the Danube, I invited a policeman from the Kladovo police station to accompany me to the site to investigate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately what time of day it was? Was it morning, afternoon, late afternoon? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that the officer on duty called me on the telephone around 1300 hours. It may have been a little earlier, but after 12.00. Between 12.00 and 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went out to the scene that afternoon, did you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as I was notified, I went there straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you see when you got there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: At a distance of about 20 to 30 metres from the bank, I saw something protruding from the water. It could have been a large box, that is, the trailer part of a truck. A closed container. It was just the tip of the trailer box.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say it was just the tip, was there a lot of it visible? Could you identify from where you were on the road what it for sure was at that point?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: You could assume that it was a lorry, a trailer with a closed container behind, inside the river, in the water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw that, what happened next? Did you give instructions to anyone to do something or did you investigate in some way to see whether it was in fact a truck or a lorry?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The diver put on his equipment and dived into the water, and when he re-surfaced, he told me that it was a lorry, that there was no one in the cab, that the front windshield had fallen out, and that it was probably a Mercedes lorry and its trailer box looked like that of a refrigerated lorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time of day was it now?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It might have been around 1600 hours, because the diver took rather a long time to get ready to dive to view the vehicle under water, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the water level in the Danube at that particular time? Was it a high river or low or was there run-off or can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly right now, but I think the level of the water was slightly above average at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any photographs that afternoon or evening of the 5th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think I took any photographs then because it was getting dark by that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since it was getting dark and since you had found there were no occupants in the cab, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The diver went in again and used a length of rope and a plastic bucket to mark the location so that we could return in the morning and find the place in case the water level rises and the object moves. I think we tied it with this rope; I'm not sure about that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after having checked it out and marking the location of the vehicle since it was getting dark, did you leave for the evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you intended to return the next day. Did you do so, and if so, what did you do upon your return?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That evening, we made arrangements for a crane to be given to us from the hydro power plant of Djerdap to help us pull out the vehicle from the water. And the next morning, the same diver, a colleague of mine from the police force, and myself went there again. The crane was already there together with ten or 15 employees of the hydro power plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was accomplished with the crane? Were you able to lift the vehicle out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Slowly, step-by-step, we pulled the lorry out. The diver got into the cab and tried to straighten the wheels by turning the wheel, and the wheels were stuck in the mud on the bottom of the river, and it took a long time and a lot of effort to pull it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You finally managed to get it to the edge of the river bank, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at some time after that had been accomplished, did you start to take photographs of this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did. On the 6th of April, when I returned to the site, I made several photographs of the vehicle in the position in which it was originally found and then another series of photographs showing progressively the process of pulling it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And of the photographs that you took that day, I now have -- that day and the next, I now have a series of ten photographs that you've supplied to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the bundle of photographs at this point, please. My proposal, Your Honours, is to mark these as one exhibit and have them marked. They actually are labeled 1 through 10, and they bear our internal numbers K0226128 right through to the last one, 6137. If that meets with your approval, rather than giving them separate exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit number 275.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've seen these photographs? These are the photographs that you took on the 6th and 7th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, looking at the first photograph, numbered 1, it's now on the ELMO, you see it there? Can you point out to us -- there's not too much to point out. Is this the first photograph that you took after of the vehicle had been dragged, by the crane, out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is the first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the second photograph. Is that a close-up of the same truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From a shorter distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, sir, when you attended the evening before, the 5th of April, can you perhaps indicate with your pointer how much of this vehicle was visible to you when you attended the day before, before the truck was pulled out of the water level? Could you perhaps just show us with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. You see this dark strip here, the right upper corner of the side of the lorry. This was made by the dirt in the water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we're looking at the lorry box, as it were, the triangle that is left by that black mark, only that top little triangle was visible to you? The rest of the vehicle was submerged?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Turning to the third photograph, sir, is that a close-up of the vehicle once it's been pulled even further out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The rear wheels are already on the bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to spend just a little bit of time with respect to this photograph. When you looked at this truck, what, if anything, did you note about the back of the -- the door area of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that the right half of the door had been broken into, that through this slit, there were two human legs and one arm protruding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's difficult to see on the screen, but could you use your pointer -- first of all, are any parts of the bodies that you've just described visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see one leg. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're now pointing just to the left of the little stair hanging down from the right corner of the box of the truck; is that correct? There is what appears to be a foot immediately to the left of that. Could you put your pointer right on the object that you say is a leg.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the object. This, the body part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with respect to that body part or any other body parts?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I have to add that the diver had informed me even before the rear of the truck was pulled out that there was a hole in the rear of the truck and that something was protruding, something that looked like a human foot or an arm, and he asked me what to do. He told me it was still in the water. And I said, "Well, there's nothing you can do. Let's pull it out and see." And when the rear of the lorry was pulled out onto the bank of the river, I saw this one foot protruding, and there were another foot and an arm less visible right there. I pushed them back inside the lorry. I fastened the interior using some planks I had handy and some nuts and bolts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you pushed the body parts back inside and then attempted to cover up the hole, did you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, once you had done that, sir, what time of day is it now on the 6th of April? Has some time passed?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was already 12 or 1300 hours by that time, maybe even later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend the scene only with a diver or did other police officers or other officials also come to the scene of this, where you found the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I had a colleague with me also from the crime investigations department, and there were two other policemen who controlled traffic on the road, and there were ten employees from the hydroelectrical power plant who operated the crane, the other equipment. I must say that when the lorry was pulled out, just before it was pulled out onto the bank, we informed the investigating judge, the coroner of the medical centre in Kladovo, and the office of the public prosecutor to come to the scene and to witness the final stages of extraction of this refrigerated lorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you called for them once you realised that this vehicle actually contained bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wait for their arrival or did you do something in the meantime? After putting the body parts back in and covering the hole, did you wait for their arrival or did you do something further?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think we did anything else. We were waiting for the investigating judge and the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they far away, and did it take them long to arrive?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't wait long. I think they actually arrived a short time before the lorry was pulled out finally onto the bank, because the extraction was extremely difficult and slow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I'd like you to turn to the next photograph, if you would, please. There appears to be a photograph of that same truck before you covered the hole but it seems to have a chain on it. Was it in that condition when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Along the centre of the door, somewhere in the middle, they were secured with a padlock and a chain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you do in regards to that chain and why?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When the investigating judge and the public prosecutor arrived, I tried to cut this chain but I failed, so I had to break through to break the padlock in order to open the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you accomplished that objective, and were you able then to open the doors to this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I opened the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw when you opened the doors.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw a heap of corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw that, what did you do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When I saw that, I shut the door immediately, and I informed the investigating judge, who was close by, about the contents of the lorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any instructions or any indication as to his interest or lack of it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The judge asked me how many bodies there were inside. I answered there were a lot. And then the judge said it was not within the purview of the court in Kladovo. A case like that was not within their jurisdiction and that we should inform the district court in Negotin. I offered to open the door for him to see what's inside, but he declined, and he said there was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: He told the policemen to seal off the site, and I went to the police station in Kladovo together with my colleagues from the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you shut the doors again, did you show any of your colleagues what was inside this box?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One or two of my colleagues saw the inside when I opened the door, and perhaps some others saw it from a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, I understand you then shut the doors again. You'd covered the hole, as you indicated. Did you secure -- did you secure the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The employees of the hydro power plant used a cable to tie the chassis of the lorry to a large tree on the bank of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to go very quickly and lead you through this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. It's time for the break. Mr. Radojkovic, we're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes. Could you remember in this and any other breaks there are in your evidence not to speak to anybody until it's over about it, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Could you be back, please, in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, just before the break you had just told us that after calling the local officials down to have a look and they declined to do so, you showed your colleagues what was in the truck and then you closed the doors and then you -- I understand you eventually went to the police station. Just before you did that, did you take some more photographs of the doors of this truck? And if so, would you please look at photographs number 5 and 6. Would you look over there.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I made a few more photographs. This was while the truck was being dragged out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And on the passenger's side, if I can call it that, of this door, we see some lettering. And if you will turn to photograph number 6, we see it a little closer. Was that the condition that the door was in on the 6th of April, as it was being taken out of the Danube River?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in this state. The front wheels were still in the water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it that it says on the door? We can read it, but perhaps you could read it for us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the door, it says the following: "PIK Progres Export Slaughterhouse. Telephone number, telefax number, Prizren."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you noticed any licence plates on either the front or the back of this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't any licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, sir, after you secured the scene, do I understand that that particular day, the 6th of April 1999, you returned to the police station?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got there, sir, did you advise the people in charge of the police station what you had seen and what you had done?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did inform the head of the local police there, the chief of the crime prevention service in the police station in Kladovo. The two of them, at any rate. I don't know if any of their associates were present as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the SUP in Kladovo was Vukasin Sperlic. The head of the group for combatting crime was Stevanovic, and Nena Popovic, Momcilo Sujranovic, my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after giving your report, did you receive any instructions with respect to what further steps, if any, you ought to take?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to customary procedure, we sent a letter to the Secretariat of the Interior, that is to say the regional SUP in Bor. We sent a written report as to what we had found in the Danube and what was in the truck. In view of the fact that all of this during the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, the entire event was taking place right by the border with Romania. And Romania had then allowed the use of their own air space for NATO aircraft very close to the site where this occurred, it's perhaps only 1.000 metres away, that is a very short distance in terms of waterways. On the Romanian side, there were Romanian patrol boats and bigger ships. Bearing in mind the fact that they had the technical devices to see this truck and perhaps even see the lettering on the door, and also bearing in mind the fact that this was close to the town of Tekija and that this lettering on the truck may be reminiscent of certain events in Kosovo, we agreed during the night that we should cover the lettering on the door so that perhaps due to that lettering we would not have any consequences by way of bombing or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you told or -- to do something or did you make a decision on your own to do something?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that I should somehow cover this lettering so that it could not be seen from a distance, so that the public could not see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Directly, I don't know. It was at local police level. So it was the head or the chief of group. That is how we agreed as to how this should be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a consequence, what, if anything, did you do later that evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later that evening, I got some car paint, and the colour was similar to that of the truck, and in the evening, I went to the site. It was during the night. So I used this car paint spray to cover the lettering on the driver's door and on the passenger's side door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although we can only see on photographs 5 and 6 of Exhibit 275 the lettering on the passenger's side door, was there similar writing on the driver's side door?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, identical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went back at night with cans of spray paint and what, if anything, did you do in relation to the writing on the doors of this truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I sprayed the writing on the door with this spray paint so that it could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told us earlier there were no licence plates on the vehicle. Did you do something in relation to licence plates?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: From the police station in Kladovo, I took some old licence plates with -- Bor licence plates, and then I damaged them a bit to make them less noticeable. And then that same night when I was spraying the doors with the spray paint, I put the licence plates on the back and on the front of the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you went home?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return the next day and take some more photographs?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning, I went to the scene again, again with my colleagues from the Kladovo police, and there was already a big group of workers from the hydroelectric power plant there, and there was also a crane there, bigger than the one that was there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about -- well, you took some photographs, and I'd like you to look at photographs number 7 and 8, if you would, please. First of all number 7, which is now on the ELMO. That's a photograph you took, and that's the same truck as the one you found on the 5th and the 6th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now there's no writing visible on the doors; is that it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are black and white photographs. Do you remember what colour the cab of this vehicle was?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you use a dark green or did you use a green matching spray paint to cover the door?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't get the right shade. Not exactly the right shade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you effectively covered up the writing; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at photograph number 8, did you -- where did you say you put the licence plate? Was it on the front or the back or both? I don't recall. Is there a licence plate showing on the back? I don't see it if -- perhaps you can help us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the front it was tied with a wire, and in the back I attached it with some nuts and bolts. But the licence plate was considerably damaged, so you couldn't really see it from afar. You'd have to go very close in order to see what it said. I had scraped off some of the paint and lettering and I had hit it with a hammer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also cover it with dirt or anything?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mud from the Danube. I smeared it with that when I put it on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the licence plate in fact now visible on the back of this vehicle, and if so, could you point out where it is, because it's not readily discernible to my eye. Could you show it to us, please.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that in the photograph you can't even see it, but it was on the lower left-hand corner. The photograph was not taken with a flash, but at any rate, it was in the lower left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could show us in photographs 9 or 10. You also took two more photographs that day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the licence plate, this white thing here, this white line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: A bit wider. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it shows -- these photographs, 9 and 10, also clear show that you've done something to the back to cover it up. Did you attach that -- what appears to be a patch on the back right rear door?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, you'd met with the local police, and did police attend the scene of this truck on the 7th of April, after you took these photographs and after the crane, the larger crane, pulled it further out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's my fault. I understand that on the 7th, you've just told us about photographs you took. You've told us that a larger crane was there. Did you use this larger crane to pull this vehicle right out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the crane -- the larger crane that was there on the 7th, was it used at all? Do you understand my question or am I phrasing this badly?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the scene itself, we first had a smaller one. It was big, but it was not big enough to pull something this big out, or this heavy out. So then the next day, an even bigger crane was brought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And what, if anything, was done with that bigger crane?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: With the larger crane, we were trying to extract the truck from the water once again. In order to make this clear, the hydroelectric power plant is very close, ten kilometres away. And then the water level goes up and down a metre or two. So then during the day, we pull out the back part and then the water goes up and then part of the truck is submerged again. So that's why we needed this bigger crane, to pull it out completely to a place that was a certain distance away from the water edge itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, sir, was at some time during that day, by use of this new, second, larger crane, did you accomplish that objective? In other words, did you get the truck out of the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did something happen that evening? Did the district police arrive?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were informed about what had happened in Kladovo and what was found on the Danube. And then the head of the district police, with his associates, came to Kladovo. When they found out about this, we were ordered to stop all activities related to the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then what?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of regional police, of district police, had a meeting in Kladovo with the local police, with his associates, and then we were informed that I and a few of my colleagues should be ready in the evening, that we should come to the police station in the evening so that we would do something in relation to the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wait until evening?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That meeting was held around 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was discussed and decided, if anything, at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was not present at the meeting. Perhaps I was in that office for about five minutes around the middle of the meeting, but I was told to get some of my colleagues who were free so that we would go during the night to get the corpses out of the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the district police and this entire team that was there. The head of the district police was, of course, the ranking member present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Caslav Golubovic. He's a colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you in fact follow those instructions and go back to the scene and remove the, as you call them, corpses from the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not only I, there were about 15 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And this is after 8.00 at night. Was it light or dark?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was dark. It was around 2300 hours in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you waited until it was dark in order to accomplish that task?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, one of the reasons was precisely because this was the time when Yugoslavia was bombed. And secondly, we had to carry out some preparations after this meeting in order to be able to go to the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you went back to the truck. I take it you opened the doors again and at that point you started removing bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw. Tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We gave assignments to different people as to what each and every person should do. I was in the refrigerator truck together with a colleague. We were extracting the corpses from the truck. One colleague was right next to the refrigerator truck, behind us, and he was taking the corpses from us and wrapping them. Others were carrying them, somebody was lighting the ground, and others were putting the corpses onto a truck. So that is how we organised the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally were inside the truck where the bodies were; is that correct? You saw them in their state in the back of the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I and another colleague and the one who was behind the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies did you remove that night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Thirty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken and how? You've described how you passed them from person to person, wrapped them. Where were they taken once they were out of the back of your truck -- or the truck you found?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where they were driven, but the truck on which the corpses were loaded went towards Milanovac, which is upstream in relation to the Danube River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your answer, am I correct in assuming that they were taken off the lorry found in the river and placed on a different truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've just told us that that truck left in the direction that you described; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, anything about those 30 bodies that you personally handled in terms of what they looked like, how they were dressed, and approximate ages or sex?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: There were both male and female bodies. As for the age pattern, I know for sure that there were two children, a boy about five or six years old and a little girl about eight or nine years old. There weren't any more children. As for the other corpses, their ages ranged from about 20 until about 70, perhaps even a bit more than that. I came to that conclusion on the basis of their external appearance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they dressed, and if so, in what type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, they were dressed. The men wore regular type of clothes; trousers, jeans, nothing special. As for the female corpses, most of them had pantaloons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "pantaloons," was there anything special about that garment?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing special, but it is characteristic of certain groups of women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of groups of women did you have in mind when you noted that clothing?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Pantaloons are not compulsory clothing for any particular group of any ethnicity, but it is certain groups, certain ethnicities that wear such clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Are you able to tell us, in your mind, what types of ethnicities are more common to wear that type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, such clothing is worn by Romany women, Turkish women, Albanian women, Muslim women. I'm not sure about other groups, whether they wear that, because we have quite a few different ethnic groups so I'm not sure whether there are others that wear them as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that there were two children and the rest were adults, and you've given us the range in age that you estimated. Could you tell what state these bodies were in? In other words, from your experience of some 25 or more years, could you tell, in your opinion, the approximate -- how long these bodies had been dead?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In my estimate - but I would like to say that I'm not a forensic expert but I'm speaking on the basis of my own experience - I can say that these corpses were not older than two or three days in relation to the day when they were found. That is to say that death had occurred two or three days before they were found in the Danube. I'm bearing in mind the fact that the water was cold, that the weather was rather cold, and that considerably effects changes on dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question about how they were dressed. Did any of them, of the bodies that you personally handled, appear to be wearing a uniform of any type at all?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look at the bodies themselves with respect to any signs as to perhaps how they might have met their death? In other words, were there any wounds or anything visible to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As for these first 30 bodies, I had a look at most of them out of curiosity or due to my profession. Those were the corpses where I had time to see the corpses because the people who were carrying the corpses were running a bit late so I helped my colleague who was wrapping up the corpses in a sheet or in a blanket or whatever, so I managed to see then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see about these bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Injuries on the bodies. Most of them were readily visible. They were mostly inflicted by something mechanical, a blunt object, but it also had to be heavy. Or a mechanical instrument but with a sharp edge. That would also have had to be heavy as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you note any gunshot wounds or bullet wounds on any of the bodies that you handled that night, the 30 bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can say something only about one of the bodies, a male body aged between 17 and 20. He was wearing jeans, and he didn't have any clothing on the upper part of the body, and he had an exit -- an entry/exit wound in the chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about his hands?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: His hands were bound with wire in the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So his hands were tied behind his back with wire; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us that it's night, it's after 11.00 or thereabouts. What kind of lighting was available to you in order to make the observations you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the refrigerator truck, we had one torchlight, and the colleague next to us, next to the refrigerator truck, the one who was wrapping up the bodies, he also had a torchlight, but they were not very strong because we didn't want to be seen from Romania. So we used this only for a short while. And I think that there was plenty of moonlight too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, did you give a detailed account of your observations, in more detail than you've told us today, to the working group of the MUP in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I provided a more detailed report to the working group. Basically it is the same as what I have said now. Perhaps it contained a little more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, if that report hasn't already been marked as an exhibit -- I believe it has been marked as an exhibit and it's found in -- I'll ask some more questions while I get the number for your reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the -- did you do anything further after you loaded these 30 bodies into the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you stop?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We did nothing more that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there more bodies still in the truck found in the Danube?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were, but around 3.00 a.m. we stopped for the time being because the workers were tired. Nobody had any strength any more. Everybody was exhausted. It was a difficult job to carry these bodies uphill. The terrain was steep, and we simply couldn't go on any more for the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return the next day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We did. We returned immediately the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to speed things up a little bit. I understand, sir, that with the crane you --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You loaded the -- you actually managed to pull this truck and put it onto a flatbed truck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, a flatbed truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you do anything during the course of the day, while it was light, with respect to the remaining bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Nothing was done with the corpses. They were only removed or, rather, the entire refrigerator lorry was pulled out, uphill out of the river onto a site where the flatbed truck was standing ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do something further with the balance of the bodies in the truck later that day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That night when dark fell, we transferred all the remaining bodies from the refrigerator lorry to the flatbed truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you wait until dark?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Because the lorry and the flatbed truck were near a very busy road from Belgrade to Kladovo. The traffic was very busy. And the other reason, as I already explained, was the vicinity of the Romanian border and their vessels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By way of summary, is it fair to say that you did not want to be seen doing what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you empty the lorry, or the truck in the Danube, did you empty the balance of the bodies at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We removed all the remaining bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The second night we removed 53 bodies which were entire bodies, if I can put it that way, and we recovered another three corpses or, rather, body parts belonging to three corpses. At least, there were three human heads and whether all of the body parts were there on the truck to make complete three corpses, I don't know. So on the whole, there were 56 bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is a fair way of summarising that to say there were 56 heads, 53 of which had bodies attached to them, intact, and body parts for the remaining three but you don't know if they made complete bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell the Court, again, how they were dressed, if they were dressed, the sex and age?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Those 53 corpses that had been removed from the refrigerator lorry the second night were also of both genders. The clothing was as I described earlier, but there were no younger people or children among them. In fact, I could say that there was no one below 20. All the bodies belonged to adults.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How -- you say all adults. Are you able to give an upper range of the age of people? Were there any elderly among them?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were people who could have been 60 or 70, judging by their faces, by their general appearance. That's the only thing I had to go by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple more quick questions about the bodies. Again, you told us that there were dressed similarly. Any uniforms on any of these 53 bodies or 56 heads?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any photographs of these bodies either the night of the 6th or the night of the 7th as you were removing them from the truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us you took bodies out on the night of the 6th and then again on the night of the 7th. Did you take any photographs of any of the bodies that you removed on either night?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When the chief of the district police arrived and that meeting was held at the police station in Kladovo, it was said that no further photographs were to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was said to whom?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: To me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under normal circumstances in the course of your duties, would it be a normal thing for you to take photographs?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you finished loading these bodies, what happened that night? Did you go home or go back to the police station, or what did you do when you finished that job?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The lorry with the corpses went further up the river again, in the direction of Donji Milanovac, and I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened, if anything, to the truck that had been found in the Danube that had been loaded onto the flatbed? Did it stay at the scene or did it leave somewhere too?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When I set out to go home, the truck was still there. But the next morning, when I came back to the police station in Kladovo, I was told that the flatbed truck, escorted by two policemen, was transported to Petrovo Selo, which is near Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any instructions by anyone with respect to the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The next day, the chief of police from Bor, or one of his associates, gave us a ring and said that this truck needs to be destroyed. It was suggested that this should be done by burning it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the suggestion. Did you receive an instruction to destroy it or what happened?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: When I received the instruction to destroy the lorry, I went to Petrovo Selo accompanied by a colleague, and we poured petrol over the lorry and set it on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the lorry?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was in Petrovo Selo, which is a village on a mountain near Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know where it was? How did you know where to go?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: This colleague of mine who accompanied me on this mission to torch the truck, he had accompanied the transfer of the lorry from Kladovo to Petrovo Selo the night before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you poured petrol on the refrigerator truck, did that destroy it sufficiently? After you set it on fire, of course.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The skeleton of the lorry remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what, if anything, did you do next?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I called up the chief of police in Bor. I told him that things were not good, that it was not going to be done that way, not going to be accomplished that way and that we had to blow it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and how?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 8th of April when we set the lorry on fire. So it must have been the 9th when we used explosives to destroy it completely. Explosives used in industry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you brought those explosives with you for the purpose of blowing up the truck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It had been brought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the explosives do the trick?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that would have happened, then, on the 9th of April, if I've been following the progression correctly, 1999.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All these events happened on several days in sequence, over several days. So it must have been Saturday, the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, a couple of years later, May 1st, 2001, did you become familiar with an article that was published in the "Timok Crime Review" in relation to that vehicle that you had discovered and dealt with?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to make a long story short, were you then questioned by the working group of the MUP? And you've already told us you've given them a report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They conducted an interview with me. I didn't give them any report. They just interviewed me and, on the basis of that interview, they drew up an Official Note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity of reading that Official Note?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I did, but only later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I promised to give you this exhibit number. You have that as Exhibit 274, that last binder that went through the previous witness, Karleusa, at tab 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had -- much later, had an opportunity to read that Official Note. Is the Official Note an accurate rendition of your recollection of what you told the working group as to what you did?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any changes at all to your -- to your statement about the communique released by the working group about what you had seen? Did you want to make any changes to that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the Official Note drawn up by the working group based on their interview with me, I stand by the contents of that Official Note in full. And at any rate, they -- the investigators got hold of this Official Note through the Ministry of the Interior. I only have reservations about the second part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the document you read, did you note anything at all about a sentence about KLA uniforms being found on any of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. That is not in the Official Note made on the basis of the interview with me. But an error must have been made later, in one of the subsequent documents, and I told them to correct it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the communique that was released; is that correct? Or do you know what document it is?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, your evidence is that on none of these 83 bodies, or 86 bodies, you saw no uniforms at all?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two more questions. The negatives -- these photographs that you've taken, some of which were entered in these proceedings, the ten photographs, you personally developed those photographs, did you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This roll of film which I used to photograph the object, I developed the film and it was part of my case file kept in my office. In 2001, I gave this negative to the working group, headed by Captain Karleusa, and he must still have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question, sir: Looking back on what happened in April of 1999, how do you feel about the way in which you were instructed to carry out that investigation? Is that a normal way that you as a professional crime scene investigator would conduct an investigation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm testifying here about what I did, what I did with my own hands, what I saw with my own eyes. As for my feelings, I had none at the time. There was a war going on. That's what had to be done. That was the way it had to be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Cross-examination tomorrow morning. Mr. Radojkovic, would you be back, please, 9.00 tomorrow morning, to conclude your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
